[quote=montfleur;61619710]Eleonore what is the situation? Asked Henri as he walked into the situation room of the Montfleurois royal palace, various generals and military advisers had already gathered and were watching Montfleurois and Rosenmarkket newsfeeds showing aerial views of Tharkønn and views of the shooting.

Forty three dead, sixty five injured, thats what we have as of now, replied Eleonore not taking her eyes off the screen.

F-cking hell, theyre shooting their own citizens now,  stated Henri, rubbing his forehead.

Intelligence suggests one of the protestors threw a stone at one of the soldiers, said one of military advisers.

F-cking hell, do they not have an escalation ladder? Asked Henri.

Eleonore shook her head, No idea,

Is there any word from the government yet, asked Henri.

No, as to be expected, they have remained silent, she replied.

Well we now have an ICJ case, sighed Henri.

Sh-t, he said sitting himself in the chair.

Have you a statement prepared? Asked Eleonore.

Uh yes, its rough but yes, replied Henri.

Sir, we have received word that military police have just detained the duke of Belgarde, said one of the advisers putting his phone down, From the consulate in Vierne,

We can do something because of that? Right ellie? Asked Henri, pointing at the adviser while looking at Eleonore.

I believe so, the duke is technically a foreign diplomat, even though half of his duchy is in Rosenmarkke, 

Its a breach of the act of settlement? Pressed Henri.

Id have to get the legal team on that one sir, she replied.

Alright, lets get to that, phone our representative to the International Forum, and lets call a joint legislative session, what are our military options? asked Henri, looking as some of the advisers gave him shocked looks.

Sir, that would stuttered one.

I know it would break neutrality, but one of our own nobles has just been arrested, people are being shot in the streets, now is not the time for moral grandstanding! I need options immediately, he snapped.

We have the gendarme on standby, replied one of the advisers resolutely.

Finally, clapped Henri, Someone who knows what the hell to do, come on people, and for lands sake, can someone get me a coffee and a vicodin! declared Henri as he sat down at the conference table.[/quote]

[b]July 17, 2028: Strømm responds[/b]

Haakon Strømm stood at the window of the Palace of the Citizens (home to the mayor of Vysjllá) staring out on the square of angry citizens and protestors that had gathered, a group of nervous soldiers barely holding the crowd back, he had prepared a speech for the protestors, calling for order and for unity, even though an itch in the back of his mind knew that the nation had gone far from that.

He turned away from the window, towards the staff that stood by the doors, nodding at them slowly, and then at his wife, he moved out onto the balcony, and waved at the crowd, who roared in anger shoving once more at his guards, he frowned as he stepped up to the microphones that had been set up on the balcony, waving at the cameras that sat on the rooftops of the buildings surrounding the square.

After waving at the people he then began to speak in a firm tone, Citizens of this peoples Republic, the disorder and chaos which has fallen across this nation, is unacceptable, the disorganisation of the armed forces command, the economists, and local governments must be ended. After an initial investigation into yesterdays events, it has come to light that the mayor of the city of Tharkønn gave the order for the soldiers to shoot upon the first sight of violence. he paused and tilted his head as the crowd continued their angry jostling and shouting, he shifted tone, We will not stand for disorder, for rowdy behaviour, for terrorism, the terrorists who attacked our armed forces were executed as they shouldve been! The republic shall stand upon the pillars of Strømmism! The traitors who demand that we cede ourselves back to the Montfleurois terrorists shall be caught and punished! Order shall return! Order shall return! 

He waved again at the cameras in a slow dignified manner before continuing, though he had begun to tremble slightly, The Wuloosyan threat shall be defeated, the sun shall rise over Rosenmarkke! Rosenmarkke shall not fall! IT SHALL NOT FALL! by this point he had realised his speech had become fruitless, and with one more wave, he retreated back into the palace, with a shake of his head.

Disperse the crowd general, he said as he walked out of the room, nodding at one of the officers (who wasnt a general) in the room.

[i]A Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 drove through the empty coastal highway, the engine echoing the silence of the night. The road stretched endlessly along jagged cliffs, waves crashing far below in the darkness. No headlights. No traffic. Just the hum of the car and the whisper of the ocean wind.

Inside, the radio crackled an old, nearly forgotten diss track playing louder than necessary.

Radio
Did you ever notice how you look at me,
but turn away like a ghost of your past

Do you remember the wall that kept us apart?
I felt it even when we were young.

Look at the stars..you gave me that same look.
The happy times I wish they were real.

On the lost page of history, forgotten and torn

The music abruptly cut to static.

Without warning, the cars headlights shut off.

Darkness swallowed everything.

The Challenger veered sharply off the main road, tires crunching over gravel as it climbed a narrow, unfinished path. The route twisted upward toward a lone structure of a rotting shack perched dangerously close to the edge of a cliff, hidden from any passing traveler.

The engine died.

Silence.

The driver stepped out, the car door slamming shut with a hollow echo. The wind picked up, carrying the scent of salt and decay.

Then

THUD! THUD! THUD!

The trunk rattled violently.

A muffled struggle from inside.

The man sighed, almost amused.

Guess someones awake from their nap.

He walked to the back of the car and lifted the trunk.

Inside, a man lay bound, wrists tied tight, a cloth stuffed in his mouth.

MMMM! MMM!!

The kidnapper crouched down, casually flipping through a file he pulled from his coat.

Lets see he muttered. Mr. Klaus. Five feet tall, age thirty five and officially declared dead.

He chuckled.

Thats funny. I dont remember my job mentioning that part.

He reached in and yanked the cloth from Klauss mouth.

Klaus gasped for air, then immediately snapped

Who the hell are you?! Who sent you?!

The man stepped back, unfazed.

Well, thats not very polite, he said dryly. Especially considering you almost shot my damn hand off earlier.

He closed the file and tapped it against his palm.

But I suppose introductions matter. A slight grin crept across his face. Names Kallus.

He paused,  looking at Klaus carefully.

I work with an independent group. We take contracts. Find people. Deliver results.

Klaus glared at him.

What do you want with me?

Kallus tilted his head.

Oh, not you.

A brief silence passed as the wind howled across the cliff.

I was hired to find someone else.

He leaned closer, his voice dropping just enough to carry weight.

A leopard girl.

Klaus froze. Felt a deepening shock. 

Kallus noticed and smiled.

Yeah, he said softly. You know exactly who Im talking about.

The waves below crashed harder, as if the ocean itself was listening.
Then Klaus started laughing.
Slow. Unstable.
He pushed himself up onto his knees, blood already drying on his lips.
Let me guess he said, grinning through pain. Youre here to kill her?
His eyes sharpened.
Because I am her loyal servant until I die.
He coughed.
Its been years since I last saw her face.
Kallus didnt respond.
Instead, he slowly pulled out a revolver.
Save the speech, he said coldly. Tell it to someone who cares.
BANG!
The shot rang out.
The bullet tore past Klauss head, ripping through his ear.
Klaus collapsed to the ground, screaming, blood spilling down the side of his face.
Kallus stepped over him, raising the revolver casually.
With his hand, he removed his hat.
Underneath
A horn like deer.
And the face of a fox.
Klaus spat blood, laughing weakly.
So its true, he muttered. A Hybrid Rukati
Kalluss expression hardened instantly.
Shut up, he snapped. I dont have time for your commentary.
He shoved the gun closer to Klauss face.
Where is she?
A pause.
Klaus smiled.
Take a look.
In one sudden motion, he grabbed a handful of sand from his pocket and hurled it straight into Kalluss eyes.
F!
Kallus staggered back, blinded.
BANG! BANG!
Two shots fired wildly into the darkness.
Silence followed.
Wind.
Waves.
Then nothing.
Kallus wiped his eyes, breathing sharp and controlled. His vision slowly cleared.
The ground in front of him was empty.
Klaus was gone.
Only a trail of blood remained leading toward the cliffside.
Kallus lowered the gun slightly, his expression no longer amused.
So you can still run, he muttered.
He looked out toward the dark ocean.
Far below, waves crashed violently against the rocks.
He thought he saw something move along the edge of the cliff. But Kallus smiled again.
Good, he said quietly.
This just got interesting.[/i][/spoiler]

[i][b]P I R N ─[/b][/i] On June 16, the Pirn Parliament issued a bold, and arguably unprecedented, decision for any nation in the 21st century, a move that effectively reshapes the entire country. The sweeping measure, titled the [b]Comprehensive Reform and Overhaul of Government, Law, and Constitution,[/b] widely referred to as the [b]Pirn Libre Resolution,[/b] transforms Pirn from a unitary parliamentary republic into a [i]unitary parliamentary republic with a union-style administrative structure.[/i]

Under the new framework, Pirns 13 Regions are granted limited autonomous powers, including the ability to enact regional laws and exercise certain forms of self-governance, though they remain barred from establishing their own constitutions or imposing independent taxes. The national government has also been renamed the Union Government of Pirn, reaffirming its role as the supreme central authority.

The decision aims to ease long-standing tensions between human citizens and furry citizens, tensions often aggravated when regional governors did not represent the demographic majority of their constituencies. The most prominent example is Victoria Region, where humans make up 57% of the population, yet the sitting governor is a furry, a situation that has long fueled dissatisfaction among local residents.

The reform package also amends Pirns constitution, granting humans the same political participation rights long held by furry citizens. At the same time, several landmark laws were introduced: the [b]Same-Sex Act[/b], which officially recognizing same-sex marriage with full legal protections; the [b]Pomolimo Act[/b], lowering the minimum age for voting and political participation from 21 to 18; and most notably the [b]Voluntary Military Service Act[/b], which abolishes compulsory military service and allows young citizens to enlist voluntarily. Another significant addition is [b]Citizenship Act No. 1884[/b], which grants automatic eligibility for Pirn citizenship to individuals with at least one Pirnian parent, adoptive Pirn parents, a Pirnian spouse, Pirnian mixed heritage, or, most notably, ancestral ties to Pirn predating 1945. Applicants are required only to complete a 12-month program covering bilingual English-French proficiency, Pirnian culture, society, and law.

Another landmark measure, the [b]Mercy Act[/b], establishes a humanitarian framework for refugees fleeing political persecution, ethnic or religious conflict, or any imminent danger to themselves or their families. The law underscores Pirns commitment to humanitarian values by providing temporary residence, basic English or French language training, assistance with social integration, employment support, and full legal protection akin to that afforded to Pirn citizens.

In exceptional cases, refugees who make notable contributions to Pirn society may be granted permanent residency on the path to eventual citizenship, a provision observers describe as without precedent. However, the [b]Mercy Act[/b] also imposes strict conditions: refugees are barred from entering marriages of convenience with Pirn citizens to exploit [b]Citizenship Act No. 1884[/b], must not violate civil or criminal laws, and must not engage in anti-government activities. Any such violations may result in deportation.

This reform package is considered the most comprehensive in Pirns history and is being hailed as one of the most extensive national transformations undertaken by any country in the 21st century. Implementation is ongoing, and further major changes are expected in the coming years.

[b]July 18, 2028: An address to the assembly[/b]

The events of the last half of the month had shocked the legislators of Montfleur as a country that had once been a coherent and powerful security state quickly fell to revolutionaries and anti-government factions. 

The general atmosphere in the assembly had shifted from direct opposition to an air of caution, with most parties agreeing on Montfleur beginning to move to facilitate basic humanitarian actions, however, the largest question loomed over the assembly, what if one of the Rosenmarkket Estates seceded? 

Henri was aware of this question and it was one which he and the legal team of the government had spent two days discussing and debating, now as he stood ready to give a speech on the matter and to call for a strategic motion to raise the Gendarme, he wondered what a total collapse of Rosenmarkke would look like, he walked to the podium.

Fellow friends,

I come to you today as a fellow Montfleurois, not just as your king. In the past month we have seen an aggressive political shift in our southern neighbor, Rosenmarkke, as the regime there begins to enter into the waning days of its eternal revolution. 

On July 16 that government shot citizens in the streets of its capital, unarmed protesters on account of a rock, and on that same night the duke of Belgarde, a citizen of Montfleur by agreement of the Acts of Settlement, was kidnapped by the government of Rosenmarkke.

These actions are a grave disturbance in international law and our own history, which begs to ask the question, where is the line in the sand to be drawn? Where is the red line? Members of the legislature may I remind you, that Rosenmarkke is a nuclear capable state? The threat with that fact raises the stakes beyond what Les Optimistes couldve predicted in 1932.

So today, I ask this assembly to conduct an assessment of our nation, and of the current situation in Rosenmarkke, where is the red line?

The assembly broke out into tense applause as the king bowed and then stepped off the podium, he had made his point.
